questions.question: If 31 August 2008 was Sunday, then what was the day of the week on 30 August 2012?
questions.solution:
Odd days:

A non-leap year has 365 days and a leap year has 366 days.

**Non-leap year =** 365 days or 52 weeks and 1 day. So, here the number of odd days is 1.

**Leap year =** 366 days or 52 weeks and 2 days So, here the number of odd days are 2.

Leap year between 2008 to 2012 = 2012

And,

Non leap year between 2008 and 2012 = 2009, 2010 and 2011.

So, total number of odd day between 2000 and 2012 = 3 (Total Non- leap year) + 2 (One leap year) = 5 days = 5 odd day

 
 

 
 
**Code of the day**

 If 31 August 2008 was Sunday, then what was the day of the week on 30 August 2012?

**31 August 2008 was Sunday**

=> Day on 31 August 2012 = Sunday + 5

= Sunday + 5 (odd day) = Friday

**Therefore, 31 August 2012 = Friday**

Now,

**30 August 2012 = ****31 August 2012** **– 1 day**

= Friday – 1day

= Thursday

Hence, **30 August 2012 **was **“Thursday”.**

questions.question:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

10 –15 × 9 ÷ 6 + 8 = 8
questions.solution:
According to the BODMAS rule:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2042326d26ec7b593e52bbbdd22d890b59b1e59f92be81a7235509e9af1c4625.png] 

**Option 1 :** – and ÷

**Given:**

**10 –15 × 9 ÷ 6 + 8 = 8**

**After interchange the signs;**

**10 ****÷15 × 9 - 6 + 8 = 8**

**By BODMAS rule**

**0.67 × 9 - 6 + 8 = 8**

**6 - 6 + 8 = 8**

**14 - 6 = 8**

**8 = 8 (LHS = RHS)**

Option 2 : + and ÷

Given: 10 –15 × 9 ÷ 6 + 8 = 8

After interchange the signs;

10 –15 × 9 + 6 ÷ 8 = 8

By BODMAS rule

10 –15 × 9 + 0.75 = 8

10 –135 + 0.75 = 8

10.75 –135 = 8

-124.25 = 8** (LHS ≠ RHS)**

Option 3: × and −

Given:10 –15 × 9 ÷ 6 + 8 = 8

After interchange the signs;

10 ×15 - 9 ÷ 6 + 8 = 8

By BODMAS rule

10 ×15 – 1.5 + 8 = 8

150 – 1.5 + 8 = 8

158 – 1.5 = 8

156.5 = 8** (LHS ≠ RHS)**

Option 4: + and ×

Given: 10 –15 × 9 ÷ 6 + 8 = 8

After interchange the signs;

10 –15 + 9 ÷ 6 × 8 = 8

By BODMAS rule

10 –15 + 1.5 × 8 = 8

10 –15 + 12 = 8

22 –15 = 8

7 = 8** (LHS ≠ RHS)**

Hence, the answer is **“****– and ÷”.**

questions.question: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.solution:
The logic is here is:

**1st number × (1st number + 1) = 2ⁿd number.**

Option (1): 9 : 90

Now, follow the logic:

9 × (9 + 1) = 9 × 10 = 90 = 2ⁿd number

This option follows the pattern.

**Option (2):** 7 : 56

7 × (7 + 1) = 7 × 8 = 56 = 2ⁿd number

This option follows the pattern.

Option (3): 5 : 30

5 × (5 + 1) = 5 × 6 = 30 = 2ⁿd number

This option follows the pattern.

**Option (4): 8 : 66**

**Now, follow the logic:**

**8 × (8 + 1) = 8 × 9 = 72 ****≠**** 2ⁿd number**

**This option do not follow the pattern.**

Hence, pair **“****8 : 66”** is an odd one.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**The logic followed here is:

**Square of 1st number + 1st number = second number**

Option 1 → 9 : 90 → 9² + 9 = 90

Option 2 → 7 : 56 → 7² + 7 = 56

Option 3 → 5 : 30 → 5² + 5 = 30

**Option 4 → 8 : 66 → 8² + 8 = 72 ≠ 66**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some teachers are graduates.

Some graduates are females.

All females are women.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some females are teachers.

II. Some women are teachers.

III. All women are females.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow.

questions.solution:
**Statements:**

Some teachers are graduates.

Some graduates are females.

All females are women.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a11778ad46bcc7f118ddfe14e27d202df113a73d3e9e900d33fa509ddb1633e.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some females are teachers → False (There is no direct relation given between females and teachers so it can be possible but not definite)

II. Some women are teachers → False (There is no direct relation given between women and teachers so it can be possible but not definite)

III. All women are females → False (because all females are women but all women are also females it is not definite)

Hence, **“****None of the conclusions follow”.**

questions.question:
Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

{6, 15, 27}
questions.solution:
The Logic here is as follows:

**(2ⁿd number × 2) - (1st Number ÷ 2) = 3rd Number**

**In **{6, 15, 27}

**(2ⁿd number × 2) - (1st Number ÷ 2)**

= (15 × 2) - (6 ÷ 2)

= 30 - 3

= 27 **= 3rd Number**

Now check the all options,

**Option (1) **{14, 38, 57}

**(2ⁿd number × 2) - (1st Number ÷ 2)**

= (38 × 2) - (14 ÷ 2)

= 76 - 7

= 69 ≠** 3rd Number**

**Option (2) **{4, 10, 18}

**(2ⁿd number × 2) - (1st Number ÷ 2)**

**= (10 × 2) - (4 ÷ 2)**

**= 20 - 2**

**= 18 = 3rd Number**

**Option (3) **{12, 32, 54}

**(2ⁿd number × 2) - (1st Number ÷ 2)**

= (32 × 2) - (12 ÷ 2)

= 64 - 6

= 58 ≠** 3rd Number**

**Option (4) **{8, 24, 34}

**(2ⁿd number × 2) - (1st Number ÷ 2)**

= (24 × 2) - (8 ÷ 2)

= 48 - 4

= 44 ≠** 3rd Number**

Hence, the correct answer is **"****{4, 10, 18}".**
